title: New Residential Construction (Census, October 2026 data — building permits, housing starts, completions), 8:30 a.m. ET
source: EST: census.gov/economic-indicators/calendar-listview.html fetched direct 2026-09-06 (HTTP 200, 91,396 bytes), row "New Residential Construction (Building Permits, Housing Starts, and Housing Completions) | November 18, 2026 | 8:30 AM | October 2026", release code A202611180830, reference A202610. Corroborated by the Atlanta Fed's GDPNowcastDataReleaseDates.xlsx PostedUpdates sheet, whose 2026-11-18 row reads "Housing starts" at 0.35416666 of a day (08:30 ET) — this release owns a GDPNow vintage of its own. Filed `estimate` per this lane's no-self-confirm limit on an event discovered in-sweep. Checked 2026-09-06
notes: DISCOVERED during the existing-home-sales-2026-11-12 initial-research adjacency sweep (2026-09-06), and it earns a row for the same reason its December twin did: it is the residential node's OTHER leaf. The Atlanta Fed's GDPTrackingModelDataAndForecasts.xlsx Residential sheet routes `valExHomeSales` into `FRSBKX_USNAqtr` ("Brokerage commissions") for existing-home sales, and `SplicedNewHousingConstruction` into `FRSPX_USNAqtr` ("Permanent-site") for starts — different leaves of one component, so the two prints can be read against each other rather than confused. Within this corridor it is the pairing that matters: 11-12 carries October existing-home closings into the commissions leaf and 11-18 carries October starts and permits into the construction leaf, six days apart, both reference month October. Distinguishing features beyond routineness: it is 08:30, so unlike the 10:00 prints in this corridor its surprise lands before the equity open; it shares its session with the October Pending Home Sales Index at 10:00 (NAR) and the FOMC minutes at 14:00, which is the same afternoon-owns-the-session shape the 12-09 ledger measured for the SEP decision; and it is the first vintage after the 11-17 stack (retail sales + inventories, import/export prices, industrial production, MTIS), so it is the corridor's first clean single-release read since 11-09. Impact LOW and symbols empty on the measurement that governs this whole class: across 2,514 daily sessions 2016-09-06 -> 2026-09-04 the homebuilder ETFs do not separate from baseline on housing-print days, and no house playbook (S1/S2/E1/S3/S4 + G1) is macro- or housing-keyed. Note for whoever picks this up: its December twin housing-starts-2026-12-17 was proposed by the existing-home-sales-2026-12-09 sweep on the same reasoning and is worth reading first. Proposed as an estimate; nothing here licenses an entry.
